title: Control exception
description: An approved exception is NOT a pass. It changes the intended state for a subset of the population, which is reduced coverage with an expiry - and an exception with no expiry is an undocumented control change. Modelling exceptions as records rather than as prose in coverage_basis is what makes them countable, expirable, and visible in the generated SSP.

control_id.description: Must resolve to a control in the inventory. An exception against a control that does not exist is an exception against nothing.

subjects.description: The population members this exception covers, enumerated. Never a wildcard: an exception whose scope cannot be enumerated is a scope change to the control, and it belongs in population_definition where an assessor will read it.

expires_at.description: Mandatory. There is no such thing as a permanent exception - if the intended state has genuinely changed, change the control, do not carry an exception forever.

compensating.description: What holds the risk down while the exception stands. An empty array is legitimate and is a much stronger statement than an absent field: it says explicitly that nothing compensates, which is a decision someone has to own rather than an oversight.
